# Expose workbench last-activity data for console consumption

## Description

The notebook controller already tracks per-workbench last-activity timestamps
(used by the idle culler), but that data is collected through Jupyter server
API probes and is not available on a surface the web console can read — the
console consumes the Kubernetes API only and uses no private component APIs.
This epic makes the controller's existing last-activity data readable through
the Kubernetes API so per-project idle-workbench reporting can be built in the
console without new data collection and without private API access.

## Scope

- Make the per-workbench last-activity data that the notebook controller
  already collects readable through the Kubernetes API, in a form that
  per-project reporting can consume. The exact surface is an implementation
  decision for the Workbenches team.
- Cover every workbench in a project, per project.
- No change to how activity is collected (the existing probe-based tracking
  stays as-is; only its exposure changes).
- No change to culling behavior: the idle culler continues to act on the same
  activity data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches, the per-workbench last-activity data
  tracked by the notebook controller is readable through the Kubernetes API for
  every workbench in that project.
- The exposed last-activity values are consistent with the notebook
  controller's activity tracking (the same view of activity the idle culler
  acts on).
- Existing idle-culling behavior is unaffected: workbenches are still stopped
  after the configured inactivity period.
- The exposure introduces no private-API dependency for console consumers
  (Kubernetes API only).
- If the last-activity data is already found to be readable on a
  console-accessible Kubernetes surface, this epic reduces to validating and
  documenting that access path — the acceptance criteria above still must be
  demonstrably met.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1, data-source side): provides the "sourced from the notebook
  controller's activity tracking" data that the per-project idle-workbench
  report requires.

# Expose stale pipeline-run metadata for console consumption

## Description

Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion metadata and per-run artifacts, and
pipeline runs are surfaced in the console today — but the console consumes the
Kubernetes API only, and the per-run completion-age and retained-artifact
information needed to identify stale, reclaimable runs is not established on a
console-readable surface. This epic makes that stale-run data available through
the Kubernetes API so per-project stale-run reporting can be built in the
console.

## Scope

- Make per-run completion time and retained-artifact information from
  Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata readable through the Kubernetes API, per
  project. The exact surface is an implementation decision for the RHOAI
  Pipelines team.
- Read-only exposure of existing metadata: no change to run execution, run
  completion handling, metadata retention, or artifact storage.
- Cover completed runs, including whether artifacts are still retained for
  each.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing completed pipeline runs, per-run completion time
  and retained-artifact information is readable through the Kubernetes API for
  that project.
- The exposed data matches Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- Pipeline execution, existing run listing in the console, and artifact
  retention are unaffected (read-only exposure).
- If the required stale-run data is already found to be readable on a
  console-accessible Kubernetes surface, this epic reduces to validating and
  documenting that access path — the acceptance criteria above still must be
  demonstrably met.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1, data-source side): provides the "sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines
  run metadata" data that the stale pipeline-run report requires.

# Per-project idle-workbench report in the web console

## Description

Adds an idle-workbench report to the RHOAI web console: per project, a
read-only report of workbenches sitting idle, showing each workbench's last
activity, owner, and reserved resources, so administrators can see reclaimable
workbench capacity with confidence. Last-activity values are sourced from the
notebook controller's activity tracking once that data is available on the
Kubernetes API; owner and reserved resources come from the workbench resources
the console already reads.

## Scope

- New per-project report view in the console listing idle workbenches with,
  per workbench: last activity, owner, and reserved resources.
- Data sourcing: last activity from the notebook controller's activity
  tracking as exposed on the Kubernetes API; owner and reserved resources from
  the workbench's existing Kubernetes resources.
- Read-only report: no stop, deletion, or other reclamation action is offered
  (automated reclamation is out of scope for this strategy).
- Report is visible to administrators, project-scoped.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project with workbenches, an administrator can open the
  idle-workbench report and see, per workbench: last activity, owner, and
  reserved resources (HLR-1).
- The report is scoped per project.
- Last-activity values shown in the report match the notebook controller's
  activity tracking.
- Owner and reserved-resource values shown in the report match the
  workbench's configuration.
- The report offers no reclamation or deletion action (out of scope).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): the web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last
  activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's
  activity tracking.

Adds a stale pipeline-run report to the RHOAI web console: per project, a
read-only report of completed pipeline runs older than a configurable age that
still retain artifacts, so administrators can see reclaimable pipeline-run
storage. The report is sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata as exposed
on the Kubernetes API.

- New per-project report view in the console listing completed pipeline runs
  older than a configurable age, together with their retained artifacts.
- Configurable staleness age threshold for the report.
- Data sourcing: completion times and retained-artifact information from
  Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata as exposed on the Kubernetes API.
- Read-only report: no deletion or cleanup action is offered (automated
  reclamation is out of scope for this strategy).
- Report is visible to administrators, project-scoped.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project with completed pipeline runs, an administrator can open the
  stale pipeline-run report and see the completed runs older than the
  configured age together with their retained artifacts (HLR-2).
- The staleness age threshold is configurable.
- The report is scoped per project.
- Report contents match Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata (runs shown are
  exactly the completed runs past the age threshold that retain artifacts).
- The report offers no deletion or cleanup action (out of scope).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): the web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed
  runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from
  Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
